title.value: Use of machine learning in pediatric surgical clinical prediction tools: A systematic review
title.justification: The title of the paper is 'Use of machine learning in pediatric surgical clinical prediction tools: A systematic review', which is directly mentioned in the paper's header and provides an accurate description of the content and focus of the review.
title.quote: Use of machine learning in pediatric surgical clinical prediction tools: A systematic review

extractions.description: This paper provides a systematic review of the use of machine learning in developing clinical prediction tools (CPTs) for pediatric surgery. It compares the efficacy and validity of ML-based CPTs with traditional statistical methods. The review highlights that while there is significant potential in incorporating ML into clinical decision-making, the clinical applicability and external validation of these tools remain limited. The paper calls for more standardized validation and integration of ML-based CPTs into clinical settings to leverage their full potential.

primary_category.justification: The primary focus of the paper is on machine learning applications in pediatric surgical settings, which does not directly relate to eco-responsible AI topics such as climate change, pollution, or sustainable finance.
primary_category.quote: This systematic review aims to compare the validity and clinical efficacy of ML-based to traditional CPTs in pediatric surgery.

secondary_categories.justification: The paper does not touch upon or imply any secondary eco-responsible AI topics throughout the analysis of the clinical prediction tools.
secondary_categories.quote: Therefore, this systematic review aims to examine the clinical efficacy and validity of ML-based CPTs as compared to statistical CPTs currently in use in the pediatric population.

primary_sub_category.justification: The chosen sub-categories do not fit the focus of the paper, which centers on the technical and clinical aspects of ML applications in medicine, not eco-responsibility through AI.
primary_sub_category.quote: This systematic review aims to compare the validity and clinical efficacy of ML-based to traditional CPTs in pediatric surgery.

secondary_sub_categories.justification: The paper does not address any topics that relate to eco-responsible AI, such as climate change mitigation, adaptation, science, or pollution.
secondary_sub_categories.quote: Therefore, this systematic review aims to examine the clinical efficacy and validity of ML-based CPTs as compared to statistical CPTs currently in use in the pediatric population.
